applies_why: The text adjudicates a collision in which each side presses its own chain read together against the other's Isaiah 7:14 link (CR2's 8:8 and 9:6-7 against DR3's sign-bounds at 7:16 and 8:3-4), the exact chain-against-chain situation K-C governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires' together with 'never verse by verse' -- readings: (a) the judge's final clause is the retired stating-verse test used as the operative ground of the verdict, since the sign (one verse) is found to not state the mechanism in its own words; (b) the clause merely reports the contested verse's content while UNDERDETERMINED actually rests on the level footing of the two chains named before it. I weighed (a), because the clause stands after the semicolon as the stated ground and no comparison of the chains' footing is written anywhere in the text.
why: Having named both chains, the judge rested its UNDERDETERMINED verdict on one verse's own silence -- the stating-verse test K-C retires and a verse-by-verse move -- instead of weighing the defender's chain-footing against the challenger's chain-footing.
